correctness.rationale: The source debiasing coefficients telescope exactly after the single nonzero gradient, giving \(v_t=(1-\beta_1)\beta_1^{t-1}G/(1-\beta_1^t)\) and \(u_t=(1-\beta_2)\beta_2^{t-1}G^2/(1-\beta_2^t)\). Because every later current gradient is zero, the published RMS detector is exactly zero, including its implementation floor. Optimizing the positive-\(\varepsilon\) update over finite impulse amplitudes yields the exact envelope \(R_t\), whose exponential factor is \((\beta_1/\sqrt{\beta_2})^{t-1}\), proving the iff boundary. The alternative-detector cap follows from \(\sqrt{\max\{u,\varepsilon^2\}}\le\sqrt u+\varepsilon\).

value.rationale: StableAdamW was introduced specifically as a stability intervention for changing gradient statistics, and its defining paper explicitly debates whether the RMS numerator should use the current gradient or first momentum. The theorem quantifies the exact safety tradeoff behind that design choice: current-gradient clipping completely ignores stale momentum once the signal vanishes, while the rejected momentum detector would enforce a scalar update cap. The sharp β1²=β2 boundary also gives a concrete lower limit on how aggressively the second-moment memory can be shortened relative to first-moment memory if one wants uniform impulse-tail amplitude control. The source defaults lie safely on the bounded side, so the result is a design diagnostic rather than an unsupported practical-failure claim.
